title: The Boy Who Lived
summary: On an odd day full of owls and cloaked strangers, Dumbledore, McGonagall and Hagrid leave a baby, Harry Potter, on the Dursleys’ doorstep. His parents are dead, but the dark wizard who attacked them has vanished.
details: Mr. and Mrs. Dursley of number four, Privet Drive, are proud of being perfectly normal. Vernon runs a drill company called Grunnings; Petunia spends her time spying on the neighbours; their baby son Dudley is, in their view, perfect. Their one secret is Petunia’s sister, Mrs. Potter, and her strange husband, whom they pretend not to have.

One dull Tuesday, Vernon notices odd things: a cat that seems to be reading a map, people in cloaks celebrating in the street, owls flying in broad daylight, and whispers about “the Potters” and their son, Harry. That night a tall, silver-bearded old man, Albus Dumbledore, appears on Privet Drive and dims every streetlamp with a lighter-like device. The tabby cat that has watched the Dursleys all day turns into Professor McGonagall.

They discuss the news. The dark wizard most people fear to name, whom Dumbledore calls Voldemort, went to the Potters’ home in Godric’s Hollow and killed Lily and James Potter. But he failed to kill their baby son, and somehow his power broke and he disappeared. Dumbledore has decided Harry should be raised by his aunt and uncle, his only family, far from the fame waiting for him in the wizarding world. McGonagall protests that the Dursleys are the worst sort of Muggles (non-magical people).

The huge, wild-haired Hagrid lands on a flying motorbike, borrowed from someone called Sirius Black, carrying baby Harry, who has a lightning-shaped cut on his forehead. Dumbledore leaves Harry on the doorstep with a letter. All over the country, witches and wizards raise their glasses “to Harry Potter — the boy who lived.”

title: The Vanishing Glass
summary: Ten years later, Harry sleeps in a cupboard under the stairs and is bullied by his spoiled cousin Dudley. On a trip to the zoo, Harry talks to a snake, and the glass of its tank mysteriously vanishes.
details: Nearly ten years have passed. Harry, almost eleven, lives in the cupboard under the stairs. He is small and skinny, with messy black hair, bright green eyes, taped-up round glasses and a thin lightning-shaped scar. The Dursleys told him his parents died in a car crash, and they forbid questions. Dudley, now large and spoiled, throws a tantrum because he has only thirty-six birthday presents, one fewer than last year.

Strange things tend to happen around Harry: hair that grows back overnight after a terrible haircut, a hideous sweater that shrinks until it won’t fit him, and once finding himself on the school roof while running from Dudley’s gang. The Dursleys always blame him.

Because Mrs. Figg, the cat-loving neighbour who usually minds Harry, has broken her leg, he is taken along on Dudley’s birthday trip to the zoo with Dudley’s friend Piers Polkiss. In the reptile house a large boa constrictor winks at Harry, and the two have a conversation: it was bred in the zoo and has never seen Brazil. When Dudley shoves Harry aside, the glass of the tank simply vanishes and the snake escapes.

Back home, Harry is locked in his cupboard for a long punishment. He thinks about the flash of green light he remembers from the crash, his dreams of a flying motorbike, and the odd strangers who sometimes bow to him in the street and then vanish.

title: The Letters from No One
summary: A letter arrives for Harry, addressed to his cupboard. Uncle Vernon destroys it, but more and more keep coming, until he flees with the family to a shack on a rock at sea. At midnight, on Harry’s birthday, someone knocks.
details: When Harry is finally let out, the summer holidays begin. Dudley is getting the uniform for Smeltings, his father’s old school, while Harry is to attend the local comprehensive. Then a letter arrives for Harry, written in emerald-green ink and addressed to “Mr. H. Potter, The Cupboard under the Stairs.” Nobody has ever written to him before.

Vernon snatches it, goes pale, and whispers with Petunia. They move Harry into Dudley’s second bedroom, as if afraid someone is watching. But the letters keep coming: through the mail slot, slipped inside eggs, and finally dozens pouring down the chimney on a Sunday, when there is no post.

Vernon snaps and drives the family away, ending up at a miserable shack on a rock in the sea during a storm. Harry lies on the floor counting down to midnight and his eleventh birthday. As the minute arrives, there is a tremendous knock at the door.

title: The Keeper of the Keys
summary: The giant Hagrid breaks down the door and tells Harry the truth: he is a wizard, he has a place at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, and his parents were murdered by Voldemort, whose curse failed on Harry.
details: A giant of a man bursts in: Hagrid, Keeper of Keys and Grounds at Hogwarts. He brings Harry a slightly squashed birthday cake and is horrified to learn the Dursleys never told him anything. He hands Harry his letter: he has been accepted at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry.

Hagrid explains that Harry’s parents were a witch and a wizard. A dark wizard, whose name Hagrid can barely bring himself to say, gathered followers and spread terror. He killed Lily and James, but when he tried to kill Harry the curse failed, leaving only the scar, and he vanished. That is why every witch and wizard knows Harry’s name. Hagrid doesn’t believe the dark wizard is dead, just too weak to carry on.

Aunt Petunia bursts out that she always knew: her sister Lily was a witch, the family’s favourite, and she married another “freak.” The Dursleys hid the truth hoping to squash the magic out of Harry. When Vernon insults Dumbledore, Hagrid angrily gives Dudley a pig’s tail with his pink umbrella. Hagrid lets slip that he was expelled from Hogwarts in his third year and isn’t supposed to do magic.

title: Diagon Alley
summary: Hagrid takes Harry to London to shop in Diagon Alley. Harry discovers he has a fortune at the wizard bank Gringotts, buys a wand that turns out to be connected to his scar, and meets the people of the wizarding world.
details: Hagrid explains wizard money (gold Galleons, silver Sickles, bronze Knuts) and Gringotts, the goblin-run bank. In London they enter the Leaky Cauldron, a dingy pub Muggles can’t see, where everyone wants to shake Harry’s hand, including the nervous, stuttering Professor Quirrell, who will teach him Defence Against the Dark Arts. Hagrid taps a brick wall, and it opens onto Diagon Alley.

At Gringotts the goblin Griphook takes them by rattling cart to Harry’s vault, which is full of gold his parents left him. Hagrid also collects a small, grubby package from vault 713 on secret Hogwarts business for Dumbledore. In Madam Malkin’s robe shop, Harry meets a pale, drawling boy who boasts about Quidditch, sneers at Hagrid and says children from Muggle families shouldn’t be let into Hogwarts.

Hagrid buys Harry a snowy owl for his birthday. At Ollivanders, wand after wand is wrong until one of holly and phoenix feather, eleven inches, sends sparks flying. Mr. Ollivander finds it curious: the phoenix that gave that feather gave one other, and its brother wand gave Harry his scar. Hagrid explains that the dark wizard was a Slytherin, and that Harry should not be afraid of not knowing magic yet. He leaves Harry with a train ticket for platform nine and three-quarters.

title: The Journey from Platform Nine and Three-Quarters
summary: With help from the red-headed Weasley family, Harry gets onto the Hogwarts Express. On the train he befriends Ron Weasley, meets bossy Hermione Granger and forgetful Neville, and refuses the friendship of snobbish Draco Malfoy.
details: Harry names his owl Hedwig. Uncle Vernon drops him at King’s Cross station and laughs when there is no platform nine and three-quarters. Then Harry overhears a plump woman fussing about the station being “packed with Muggles”: Mrs. Weasley, with her red-haired children. She tells him to walk straight at the barrier between platforms nine and ten, and he passes through onto a platform with a scarlet steam engine, the Hogwarts Express. The twins, Fred and George, help with his trunk and notice his scar.

Their youngest brother, Ron, shares Harry’s compartment. He has five older brothers to live up to (Bill, Charlie, Percy the prefect, and the twins) plus a little sister, Ginny, and his only pet is a sleepy hand-me-down rat called Scabbers. Ron mentions that someone tried to break into a vault at Gringotts. Harry buys the whole sweets trolley to share, and from a Chocolate Frog card learns about Albus Dumbledore, famous for, among other things, his work on alchemy with his partner Nicolas Flamel.

A round-faced boy, Neville, has lost his toad, and a bossy, bushy-haired girl, Hermione Granger, helps search. She has memorized all her textbooks and already knows who Harry is. Then the pale boy from Madam Malkin’s arrives with two thuggish friends, Crabbe and Goyle. He introduces himself as Draco Malfoy, mocks Ron’s family and offers to help Harry make the right sort of friends. Harry refuses. Scabbers bites Goyle. At Hogsmeade station Hagrid leads the first-years across a black lake in little boats to the castle.

title: The Sorting Hat
summary: The first-years are sorted into houses by a singing hat. Harry asks not to be put in Slytherin and joins Ron, Hermione and Neville in Gryffindor. At the feast, his scar burns when a hook-nosed teacher looks at him.
details: Professor McGonagall explains that each student will join one of four houses (Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw or Slytherin) which win and lose points all year in the race for the House Cup. Ghosts float through the waiting room. In the Great Hall, under a ceiling enchanted to look like the night sky, an old patched hat sings about the houses.

One by one the first-years put on the Sorting Hat. Hermione goes to Gryffindor, as does Neville; Draco Malfoy goes straight to Slytherin. When Harry’s turn comes, the hat tells him he could be great in Slytherin, but Harry silently pleads “not Slytherin,” and the hat shouts “Gryffindor!” Ron joins him to huge cheers, with the twins chanting “We got Potter!”

Dumbledore says a few odd words, and a feast appears. Nearly Headless Nick, Gryffindor’s ghost, shows how his head hangs by a sliver of skin. Seamus Finnigan and Neville describe their families. Looking at the staff table, Harry catches the eye of a teacher with greasy black hair and a hooked nose, talking to Professor Quirrell in his purple turban, and feels a sharp pain in his scar. Percy says the teacher is Professor Snape, who teaches Potions and is said to want Quirrell’s job.

Dumbledore warns that the Forbidden Forest is off limits and that the third-floor corridor on the right-hand side is forbidden to anyone who does not wish to die a very painful death. Percy leads the Gryffindors past the poltergeist Peeves to a portrait of a Fat Lady, who opens at the password. That night Harry dreams of a turban that tells him to transfer to Slytherin, a flash of green light, and high, cold laughter.

title: The Potions Master
summary: Harry struggles with the castle and his classes. In his first Potions lesson, Professor Snape picks on him relentlessly. Over tea, Harry finds a newspaper clipping: the Gringotts vault Hagrid emptied was broken into the same day.
details: Everyone stares at Harry in the corridors. The castle is full of tricks: staircases that move, doors that won’t open, and Peeves dropping things on people. The caretaker, Argus Filch, and his cat, Mrs. Norris, seem to sense rule-breakers. Classes begin: Herbology with Professor Sprout, History of Magic taught by the ghost Professor Binns, Charms with the tiny Professor Flitwick, who falls off his books of excitement at Harry’s name, and strict Transfiguration with McGonagall. Quirrell’s Defence classroom smells of garlic, said to ward off a vampire, and he claims his turban was a gift from an African prince.

On Friday the Gryffindors have double Potions with the Slytherins in a cold dungeon. Snape calls Harry “our new celebrity” and fires questions at him he can’t answer (what you get from asphodel and wormwood, where to find a bezoar), ignoring Hermione’s raised hand, and takes points for his “cheek.” When Neville melts a cauldron and gets covered in boils, Snape blames Harry for not stopping him.

That afternoon Harry and Ron visit Hagrid’s hut, with its enormous boarhound, Fang, and teeth-breaking rock cakes. Under the tea cozy Harry finds a Daily Prophet clipping: Gringotts vault 713 was broken into on Harry’s birthday, but nothing was taken because it had been emptied earlier that same day. Hagrid emptied that vault. Hagrid avoids Harry’s questions, and also brushes off his question about why Snape seems to hate him.

title: The Midnight Duel
summary: At his first flying lesson, Harry shows a natural gift and is made Gryffindor’s Seeker. Tricked into a midnight duel by Malfoy, Harry, Ron, Hermione and Neville stumble into the forbidden corridor and find a three-headed dog guarding a trapdoor.
details: Neville receives a Remembrall from his gran. At the first flying lesson with Madam Hooch, Neville loses control, falls and breaks his wrist. While Hooch takes him to the hospital wing, Malfoy grabs the Remembrall and flies off with it. Harry, who has never been on a broom, kicks off after him and turns out to be a born flier, catching the ball in a steep dive just before it hits a window.

Professor McGonagall saw it all. Instead of punishing Harry, she takes him to Oliver Wood, captain of the Gryffindor Quidditch team, and makes him the team’s Seeker, the youngest house player in a century. His father, she mentions, was an excellent player too.

Malfoy challenges Harry to a wizard’s duel at midnight in the trophy room, with Crabbe as his second and Ron as Harry’s. Hermione tries to stop them and ends up locked out of Gryffindor Tower, along with Neville, who has forgotten the password. Malfoy never comes: he has tipped off Filch. Fleeing, they end up at a locked door, which Hermione opens with a spell.

They are in the forbidden third-floor corridor, face to face with a gigantic three-headed dog. They escape back to the common room. Hermione points out that the dog was standing on a trapdoor: it is guarding something. Harry thinks he knows what: Hagrid’s grubby little package from vault 713.

title: Hallowe’en
summary: Harry gets a top racing broom and learns the rules of Quidditch. On Halloween, a troll gets into the castle; Harry and Ron rescue Hermione from it in a girls’ bathroom, and the three become friends.
details: At breakfast Harry receives a long parcel: a Nimbus Two Thousand racing broom, sent by McGonagall. Malfoy tries to get him in trouble for having it, but Professor Flitwick already knows. Oliver Wood teaches Harry the game: three Chasers score with the Quaffle through hoops guarded by the Keeper; two Beaters swat away the violent Bludgers; and the Seeker must catch the tiny, darting Golden Snitch, which ends the game and is worth 150 points.

In Charms the class learns the levitation spell. Hermione gets her feather floating at once and corrects Ron’s pronunciation; afterwards Ron mocks her as a know-it-all with no friends. She overhears and spends the afternoon crying in the girls’ bathroom.

At the Halloween feast Professor Quirrell runs in shouting that there is a troll in the dungeons, then faints. Dumbledore sends the students to their dormitories, but Harry and Ron realize Hermione doesn’t know. They see the twelve-foot mountain troll go into a room and lock it in, then hear a scream: it’s the girls’ bathroom.

They fight the troll. Harry jumps on its back and jams his wand up its nose, and Ron finally makes the levitation spell work, dropping the troll’s own club on its head. McGonagall, Snape and Quirrell rush in. Hermione lies that she went looking for the troll herself and was saved by the boys, losing Gryffindor five points; the boys earn five points each. From then on, Hermione is their friend.

title: Quidditch
summary: Harry spots Snape’s mauled leg and suspects he tried to get past the three-headed dog. During Harry’s first Quidditch match his broom goes wild; Hermione, sure Snape is jinxing it, sets his robes on fire. Hagrid lets slip the name Nicolas Flamel.
details: Snape confiscates Harry’s library book, Quidditch Through the Ages. When Harry goes to the staff room to ask for it back, he finds Snape with a bloody, mangled leg, complaining to Filch about keeping an eye on “all three heads.” Harry is sure Snape let the troll in on Halloween as a distraction while he tried to get past the dog.

At the first match, Gryffindor against Slytherin, Lee Jordan commentates while McGonagall reins him in. Gryffindor scores, Slytherin’s captain Marcus Flint fouls, and then Harry’s broom starts bucking and rolling as though trying to throw him off. Hermione grabs Hagrid’s binoculars and sees Snape staring at Harry, muttering nonstop without blinking.

Hermione races round the stands, knocking Professor Quirrell over on the way, and sets Snape’s robes on fire with a jar of blue flames. The broom stops jerking. Harry dives, nearly swallows the Snitch, and catches it in his mouth: Gryffindor wins.

Over tea, Harry and his friends tell Hagrid they believe Snape cursed the broom. Hagrid refuses to believe it of a Hogwarts teacher, and lets slip that the three-headed dog is his, named Fluffy, and that what it guards is strictly between Dumbledore and someone called Nicolas Flamel.

title: The Mirror of Erised
summary: Over Christmas, Harry receives an Invisibility Cloak that belonged to his father. Exploring under it, he finds a mirror that shows his dead parents. Dumbledore explains that it shows your deepest desire, and warns him not to dwell on dreams.
details: Harry, Ron and Hermione search the library for Nicolas Flamel without luck. Harry stays at Hogwarts for Christmas, as does Ron, whose parents are visiting his brother Charlie in Romania, where he studies dragons. On Christmas morning Harry is amazed to have presents: a flute Hagrid carved, a hand-knitted sweater and fudge from Mrs. Weasley, a fifty-pence coin from the Dursleys, and a silvery cloak that makes the wearer invisible, with an unsigned note saying it belonged to his father and to use it well.

That night Harry sneaks into the Restricted Section of the library under the cloak. A book screams when he opens it, and fleeing Filch, he slips into an unused classroom. There stands a tall mirror with an inscription across the top. In it Harry sees himself surrounded by his family: his mother, with his own green eyes, his father, with his untidy hair, and many more relatives.

He brings Ron, who sees himself as Head Boy and Quidditch captain, holding the House Cup. On the third night Dumbledore is waiting. He explains that the Mirror of Erised shows the deepest, most desperate desire of our hearts, which has driven people mad. It will be moved, and Harry must not look for it again: “It does not do to dwell on dreams and forget to live.” Asked what he sees, Dumbledore says he sees himself holding a pair of thick woollen socks.

title: Nicolas Flamel
summary: A Chocolate Frog card finally tells the friends who Nicolas Flamel is: maker of the Sorcerer’s Stone, which grants gold and eternal life. The dog must be guarding it. After a quick Quidditch win, Harry overhears Snape threatening Quirrell in the forest.
details: Harry worries because Snape will referee the next Quidditch match. Neville hops in, his legs stuck together by Malfoy’s Leg-Locker Curse; Hermione frees him, and Harry tells him he’s worth twelve of Malfoy and gives him a Chocolate Frog. The card inside is Dumbledore again, and Harry remembers where he read the name: Dumbledore’s work with his partner Nicolas Flamel.

Hermione fetches a huge old book. Flamel is the only known maker of the Sorcerer’s Stone, a legendary substance that turns metal into gold and produces the Elixir of Life, which makes the drinker immortal. Flamel is 665 years old. The three-headed dog must be guarding the Stone, and Snape must want it.

Dumbledore comes to watch the match, and Snape, refereeing spitefully, has no chance to do harm: Harry catches the Snitch within about five minutes. Afterward Harry sees a hooded Snape slip into the Forbidden Forest and follows on his broom. He overhears Snape pressing a frightened Quirrell to find out how to get past “that beast of Hagrid’s,” warning him about his “hocus-pocus” and to decide where his loyalties lie.

Harry tells Ron and Hermione his conclusion: other teachers have placed protections around the Stone, Quirrell must have cast an anti-Dark Arts spell that Snape needs to break, and the Stone is safe only as long as Quirrell holds out against Snape.

title: Norbert the Norwegian Ridgeback
summary: Hagrid has won a dragon egg from a stranger in a pub and hatches a baby dragon, Norbert. With help from Ron’s brother Charlie, the friends smuggle the dragon out at midnight, but Harry and Hermione are caught by Filch.
details: Quirrell seems braver than expected, as the Stone apparently remains safe. Exams are coming, and Hermione makes study timetables. In the library the friends find Hagrid reading about dragons. In his sweltering hut he admits he is incubating a dragon egg in the fire, won in a card game from a hooded stranger at the village pub. He also lists the protections around the Stone: spells by Professors Sprout, Flitwick, McGonagall, Quirrell and Snape, and Dumbledore’s own, besides Fluffy. Only he and Dumbledore know how to get past Fluffy.

The egg hatches into a Norwegian Ridgeback, and Malfoy sees it through the window. Hagrid names it Norbert. Dragons are illegal, and Norbert grows fast. Ron gets bitten, and his hand swells horribly, sending him to Madam Pomfrey in the hospital wing, where Malfoy borrows a book in which Ron had left a letter from Charlie.

Charlie’s friends will collect Norbert at midnight on Saturday from the top of the tallest tower. Under the Invisibility Cloak, Harry and Hermione haul the crate up, while Malfoy, out of bed to catch them, is caught by McGonagall instead. The handover goes perfectly. But in their relief they leave the cloak at the top of the tower, and Filch is waiting at the bottom of the stairs.

title: The Forbidden Forest
summary: Gryffindor loses 150 points and the whole school turns on Harry. Serving detention with Hagrid in the Forbidden Forest, Harry finds a hooded figure drinking a dead unicorn’s blood and is saved by the centaur Firenze.
details: McGonagall takes fifty points each from Harry, Hermione and Neville, who had tried to warn them about Malfoy, and gives Malfoy a detention too. Gryffindor drops from first to last, and almost everyone, even Gryffindors, turns on Harry. He vows to stop meddling. But passing a classroom, he hears Quirrell pleading “No — no — not again, please,” and guesses Snape has finally broken him. Ron and Hermione persuade him to wait.

The detention is with Hagrid in the Forbidden Forest: something has been killing unicorns. They meet two centaurs, Ronan and Bane, who only say that Mars is bright tonight. The group splits; Malfoy scares Neville into sending up red sparks, so Hagrid swaps Neville for Harry, who goes on with Malfoy and Fang.

In a clearing they find a dead unicorn, and a hooded figure crawls out of the shadows and drinks its silvery blood. Malfoy and Fang bolt; Harry’s scar explodes with pain. A young centaur, Firenze, charges the figure off and carries Harry to safety, to Bane’s fury that he has meddled with what the planets foretell.

Firenze explains that unicorn blood keeps you alive even near death, but at a terrible price: a cursed half-life. Only someone desperate enough, waiting for something that will restore full strength, like the Stone, would do it. Harry realizes what Firenze means: the figure was Voldemort, and Snape wants the Stone for him. Back in bed, Harry finds his Invisibility Cloak returned with a note: “Just in case.”

title: Through the Trapdoor
summary: Harry realizes Hagrid told a stranger how to get past Fluffy. With Dumbledore away, Harry, Ron and Hermione go after the Stone themselves, getting through a series of enchanted obstacles until Harry goes on alone.
details: Exams take place in sweltering heat, while Harry’s scar keeps prickling. Then he realizes how odd it was that a stranger happened to have a dragon egg, which is the one thing Hagrid wants most. Hagrid admits the stranger, who kept his hood up, asked about Fluffy, and Hagrid told him the secret: play it music and it falls asleep.

They rush to tell Dumbledore, but McGonagall says he has just left for London, called away by an urgent owl from the Ministry of Magic. They decide to go after the Stone that night. Neville tries to stop them, and Hermione freezes him with a full Body-Bind.

Under the cloak they find the door open and a harp already enchanted to play beside the sleeping Fluffy. Harry plays Hagrid’s flute, and they drop through the trapdoor. Hermione defeats the strangling Devil’s Snare with fire. Harry, on a broom, catches the right winged key out of hundreds. On a giant chessboard Ron directs the game and sacrifices himself so Harry can checkmate. A troll lies already knocked out. Finally, a riddle of seven potion bottles guarded by fire: Hermione solves it.

There is enough potion for only one person to go on through the black flames. Hermione drinks the potion to go back, tend Ron and send an owl to Dumbledore. Harry walks through the fire into the last chamber. Someone is already there, but it isn’t Snape. It isn’t even Voldemort.

title: The Man with Two Faces
summary: It is Quirrell, who serves Voldemort and shares his body. Snape had been protecting Harry all along. Harry gets the Stone from the Mirror of Erised and holds out until Dumbledore saves him. Gryffindor wins the House Cup.
details: Quirrell is waiting, his stammer gone. He reveals that he jinxed Harry’s broom, Snape was muttering a counter-curse to save him, and Snape refereed the next match to stop Quirrell trying again. Quirrell let the troll in on Halloween; Snape, already suspicious, went straight to the third floor to head him off. Quirrell met Voldemort in Albania and has served him since; he failed to steal the Stone from Gringotts and has been punished for it. The pleading Harry overheard was Quirrell begging his master.

The Stone is hidden in the Mirror of Erised, and Quirrell can’t work out how to get it. A high voice tells him to use the boy. Harry looks into the mirror and sees his reflection put the Stone in his pocket, and feels it really arrive there. Quirrell unwraps his turban: on the back of his head is a second face, Voldemort, who has been sharing Quirrell’s body and drinking unicorn blood to survive. Voldemort offers to bring Harry’s parents back, but Harry refuses. When Quirrell grabs him, his hands blister and burn at Harry’s touch. Harry fights on in agony until he blacks out.

He wakes in the hospital wing. Dumbledore explains: he arrived in time. The Stone has been destroyed with Flamel’s agreement, and Voldemort, who left Quirrell to die, is still out there. Harry’s mother died to save him, and love that powerful leaves its own protection, which is why Quirrell could not bear to touch him. Dumbledore sent him the cloak. Snape hated Harry’s father, who once saved his life, and has been protecting Harry to repay the debt. The mirror gave the Stone only to someone who wanted to find it but not use it.

Hagrid gives Harry an album of photos of his parents. At the end-of-year feast Slytherin seems to have won the House Cup, until Dumbledore awards last-minute points: fifty to Ron for chess, fifty to Hermione for logic, sixty to Harry for courage, and ten to Neville for standing up to his friends. Gryffindor wins. Harry goes home for the summer knowing the Dursleys don’t know he isn’t allowed to use magic outside school.
